The omakase runs to small dishes and about a dozen nigiri, with standouts like abalone steamed for six hours in its liver sauce (mixed with a little sushi rice at the end), sweet uni, medium-fatty tuna and anago with a rich sauce. The pairing pours a glass every two or three courses from a list of over 200 champagnes, with a featured house each month, and staff guide non-experts well. Dinner only, all guests start together; reserve for an anniversary night. One diner found a grilled fish watery.

Smoking allowed. Closed Wednesdays.

osaka_kinoko_no_sato_minamisenba.notes: [Mushroom · creative mushroom courses, Minami-Senba] A small, pleasant restaurant near Shinsaibashi where nearly everything at dinner is mushrooms. Staff explain the mushrooms and how to eat each dish. Seasoning is gentle and the umami is deep. Try the mushroom sake or gin. Weekday lunch is a different menu: soup curry only. Reserve for dinner. One diner got soggy tempura.

osaka_curry_ya_dekkao_minamisenba.notes: [Curry · Sri Lankan-style curry plates, Minami-Senba] A busy, homey second-floor curry shop near Shinsaibashi, easy to miss from the street, serving Sri Lankan-style curry adapted to Japanese tastes: spicy but approachable. Build a plate around the bone-in chicken curry and one or two of the four or five daily curries, such as clam and tomato or spicy coconut tuna; the Dekkao Special is ¥1,300 and the Greedy version adds a second curry and more sides for ¥1,650. Taste each curry and side first, then mix it all together. Warm, smiling staff. Expect a line at opening. Mostly lunch; dinner Tuesdays and Thursdays. Closed Sundays. PayPay, no cards.

chef_bio.philosophy: Sri Lankan curry blended with Japanese cooking to suit Japanese tastes (September 2026 review, citing the owner).

osaka_yakiniku_union_shinmachi.notes: [Yakiniku · a stylish wagyu yakiniku with fresh offal, Shinmachi] An eleven-seat yakiniku near Nishi-Ohashi with a stylish room and charming staff, where one diner reported eating well for about ¥10,000 and feeling light afterwards. Closed Tuesdays.

osaka_savatomy_azuchimachi.notes: [Chinese · a creative Chinese bar of small plates, Azuchimachi] A stylish, busy Chinese bar near Sakaisuji-Honmachi where colorful small plates are sized for two to share. The must-order is the seared bonito in the house red sauce, smoky and gently spicy; add the moist drool chicken, fluffy anago, dim sum and, in season, oyster spring rolls, with an 18-year Shaoxing wine, straight or with soda. Seasoning is balanced enough for friends who avoid heat. Lunch is a bargain, with dan dan noodles, mapo tofu or a fuller set for about ¥2,000; one weekday it was full soon after 11:30. Reserve for dinner. Closed Sundays.

osaka_men_chu_minamihorie.notes: [Ramen · an old-style chicken shoyu shop, Minami-Horie] A quiet neighborhood ramen shop in western Minami-Horie with warm, attentive staff. osaka_menya_aozora_tsutenkaku.notes: [Ramen · Hakata tonkotsu near Tsutenkaku] A calm tonkotsu shop a block from Tsutenkaku, recently moved here from Sennichimae-dori, with multilingual QR ordering and every kind of payment. The Hakata Yatai Tonkotsu (¥900) is a foamy, well-balanced bowl on thin noodles that even a tonkotsu-shy diner enjoyed; the house original, Shin Nara Tonkotsu (¥900), crosses it with Nara stamina ramen, red with chili at the spicy setting and topped with extra pork. Sets add kara-age and fried rice, though one diner found the rice pre-made. Open 11:00–23:00 daily.

osaka_ramen_cho_hiranomachi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–23:00; closed Sun and public holidays (Tabelog). Cash only (Tabelog). Garlic added only if you want it (2026).
osaka_ramen_cho_hiranomachi.notes: [Ramen · a light, cheap garlic ramen in the office district, Hiranomachi] A simple ramen shop behind a clear vinyl entrance and a bright yellow "garlic ramen" sign near Kitahama, with a tiny ground-floor counter and tables upstairs. The ramen (¥750) is light and old-fashioned, with flavorful soy-seasoned chashu; the owner asks whether you want garlic, which hides as whole cloves at the bottom of the bowl. Two diners found the garlic milder and the broth plainer than the sign promises, but it is cheap and easy after a night out. A ramen set with rice is ¥900. Cash only. Closed Sundays.

anecdotes.text: "When you order ramen here, the owner kindly asks, 'Would you like garlic with that?'… The ramen at this restaurant is very light." — May 2026, ramen ¥750.

"The flavor was light… Hidden at the bottom were some garlic cloves, which added a nice punch when eaten. The chashu was well-seasoned with soy sauce, giving it a nostalgic taste." — July 2026, Ramen Set Meal ¥900.

osaka_naniwa_gomi_hatchin_ramen_shinseka.notes: [Ramen · late-night stamina ramen and curry under Tsutenkaku] A small ramen shop at the foot of Tsutenkaku, open from 10 am until 4 am every day, that also serves Kanazawa-style Go Go Curry. The negi ramen (¥1,150) is a Tenri-style stamina bowl: a soy broth full of napa cabbage with a kick of chili and garlic, thin curly noodles and a heap of green onion; add a fluffy half fried rice for ¥300. The thick pork-cutlet curry, eaten with a fork, is the alternative. Tables at the back feel tucked away. One diner found the service inattentive. Every payment type accepted.

"Although it's primarily a ramen shop, I was intrigued to find… [it serves] 'Gogo Curry,' famous for its Kanazawa-style curry." — September 2026, pork cutlet curry.
